      "unit": "F000",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": null,
        "statement": "Section 717 of title 38, United States Code, as added by subsection (a)(1), applies with respect to any 365-day period beginning on or after December 16, 2016.",

    {
      "unit": "F004:F011",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": ["term.covered_service"],
        "statement": "The Secretary must order that the covered service of an employee of the Department removed from a position for performance or misconduct under section 713, 714, or 7461 of title 38 or any other provision of law not be taken into account for purposes of calculating an annuity with respect to such individual under chapter 83 or chapter 84 of title 5, if the Secretary determines that the individual is convicted of a felony (and the conviction is final) that influenced the individual's performance while employed in the position, and before the order is made the individual is afforded notice of the proposed order and an opportunity to respond by not later than 10 business days following receipt of notice, and the Secretary issues the order not later than 5 business days after receiving the response (if the individual responds) or not later than 15 business days after notice is provided (if the individual does not respond).",
        "actor": "Secretary",
        "actor_quote": "The Secretary",
        "kind": "requirement",
        "modality": "must",
        "scope_text": null,
        "scope_quotes": null,

        "references": ["section 713", "section 714", "section 7461", "chapter 83 of title 5", "chapter 84 of title 5"]
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F013",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": null,
        "statement": "Any individual with respect to whom an annuity is reduced under subsection 719(a) may appeal the reduction to the Director of the Office of Personnel Management pursuant to such regulations as the Director may prescribe for purposes of subsection 719(a).",
        "actor": "individual with respect to whom an annuity is reduced under this subsection",

    {
      "unit": "F016:F023",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": ["term.covered_service"],
        "statement": "The Secretary may order that the covered service of an individual who the Secretary proposes to remove for performance or misconduct under section 713, 714, or 7461 of title 38 or any other provision of law but who leaves employment at the Department prior to the issuance of a final decision with respect to such action not be taken into account for calculating an annuity under chapter 83 or chapter 84 of title 5, if the Secretary determines that the individual is convicted of a felony (and the conviction is final) that influenced the individual's performance while employed in the position, and before the order is made the individual is afforded notice of the proposed order and an opportunity to respond by not later than 10 business days following receipt of notice, and the Secretary issues the order not later than 5 business days after receiving a response or not later than 15 business days after providing notice if the individual does not respond.",

      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": null,
        "statement": "Upon the issuance of an order by the Secretary under section 719(b)(1), the individual shall have an opportunity to appeal the order to the Director of the Office of Personnel Management before the date that is seven business days after the date of such issuance.",

        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": null,
        "statement": "The Director of the Office of Personnel Management must make a final decision with respect to an appeal under paragraph 719(b)(2) within 30 business days of receiving the appeal.",
        "actor": "Director of the Office of Personnel Management",
        "actor_quote": "The Director of the Office of Personnel Management",

    {
      "unit": "F028",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": null,
        "statement": "Not later than 37 business days after the Secretary issues a final order under subsection 719(a) or (b) with respect to an individual, the Director of the Office of Personnel Management must recalculate the annuity of the individual.",
        "actor": "Director of the Office of Personnel Management",

      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": ["term.covered_service"],
        "statement": "Any individual with respect to whom an annuity is reduced under subsection 719(a) or (b) is entitled to be paid so much of such individual's lump-sum credit as is attributable to the period of covered service.",
        "actor": "individual with respect to whom an annuity is reduced under subsection (a) or (b)",

      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": null,
        "statement": "The Secretary, in consultation with the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, must prescribe regulations that may provide for the payment to the spouse or children of any individual referred to in subsection 719(a) or (b) of any amounts which (but for this subsection) would otherwise have been nonpayable by reason of such subsections; such regulations must be consistent with the requirements of section 8332(o)(6) and 8411(l)(5) of title 5, as the case may be.",

    {

      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": "term.covered_service",
        "term_refs": null,
        "statement": "In section 719, 'covered service' means, with respect to an individual subject to a removal for performance or misconduct under section 719 or 7461 of title 38 or any other provision of law, the period of service beginning on the date that the Secretary determines under such applicable provision that the individual engaged in activity that gave rise to such action and ending on the date that the individual is removed from or leaves a position of employment at the Department prior to the issuance of a final decision with respect to such action.",

        "term_refs": null,
        "statement": "In section 719, 'lump-sum credit' has the meaning given such term in section 8331(8) or section 8401(19) of title 5, as the case may be.",

        "statement": "Section 719 of title 38, United States Code, as added by subsection 203(a)(1), applies to any action of removal of an employee of the Department of Veterans Affairs under section 719 or 7461 of such title or any other provision of law, commencing on or after June 23, 2017.",

      "unit": "F049:F057",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": null,
        "statement": "Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the Secretary may issue an order directing an employee of the Department to repay the amount, or a portion of the amount, of any award or bonus paid to the employee under title 5 (including chapters 45 or 53) or title 38 if the Secretary determines that the individual engaged in misconduct or poor performance prior to payment of the award or bonus and that such award or bonus would not have been paid (in whole or in part) had the misconduct or poor performance been known prior to payment, provided that before repayment the employee is afforded notice of the proposed order and an opportunity to respond not later than 10 business days after receipt of notice, and the Secretary issues the order not later than 5 business days after receiving a response or not later than 15 business days after providing notice if the individual does not respond.",

        "statement": "Upon the issuance of an order by the Secretary under subsection 721(a) with respect to an individual, the individual shall have an opportunity to appeal the order to the Director of the Office of Personnel Management before the date that is seven business days after the date of such issuance.",

      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": null,
        "statement": "Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the Secretary may issue an order directing an employee of the Department to repay the amount, or a portion of the amount, paid to or on behalf of the employee under title 5 for relocation expenses (including any expenses under section 5724 or 5724a of such title) or under title 38 if the Secretary determines that relocation expenses were paid following an act of fraud or malfeasance that influenced the authorization of the relocation expenses, and before repayment the employee is afforded notice of the proposed order and an opportunity to respond not later than 10 business days following receipt of notice, and the Secretary issues the order not later than 5 business days after receiving a response or not later than 15 business days after providing notice if the individual does not respond.",

      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": ["term.political_appointee"],
        "statement": "The Secretary must conduct an annual performance plan for each political appointee of the Department that is similar to the annual performance plan conducted for an employee of the Department who is appointed as a career appointee (as defined in section 3132(a) of title 5) within the Senior Executive Service at the Department.",

    {
      "unit": "F094:F098",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": ["term.political_appointee"],
        "statement": "Each annual performance plan conducted under subsection 725(a) with respect to a political appointee of the Department must include an assessment of whether the appointee is meeting the goals of: (1) recruiting, selecting, and retaining well-qualified individuals for employment at the Department; (2) engaging and motivating employees; (3) training and developing employees and preparing those employees for future leadership roles within the Department; and (4) holding each employee of the Department that is a manager accountable for addressing issues relating to performance, in particular issues relating to the performance of employees that report to the manager.",
        "actor": null,

        "term_refs": null,
        "statement": "In section 725, 'political appointee' means an employee of the Department who holds either a position which has been excepted from the competitive service by reason of its confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating character, or a position in the Senior Executive Service as a noncareer appointee (as defined in section 3132(a) of title 5).",

        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": ["term.appropriate_committees_of_congress", "term.senior_executive"],
        "statement": "Not later than 100 days after the end of each fiscal year, the Secretary must submit to the appropriate committees of Congress a report that contains, for the most recent fiscal year ending before submittal, a description of all performance awards or bonuses awarded to each Regional Office Director of the Department, Director of a Medical Center of the Department, Director of a Veterans Integrated Service Network, and Senior executive of the Department.",

unit_attributes.statement: Section 717 of title 38, United States Code, as added by subsection (a)(1), applies with respect to any 365-day period beginning on or after December 16, 2016.

The Secretary must order that the covered service of an employee of the Department removed from a position for performance or misconduct under section 713, 714, or 7461 of title 38 or any other provision of law not be taken into account for purposes of calculating an annuity with respect to such individual under chapter 83 or chapter 84 of title 5, if the Secretary determines that the individual is convicted of a felony (and the conviction is final) that influenced the individual's performance while employed in the position, and before the order is made the individual is afforded notice of the proposed order and an opportunity to respond by not later than 10 business days following receipt of notice, and the Secretary issues the order not later than 5 business days after receiving the response (if the individual responds) or not later than 15 business days after notice is provided (if the individual does not respond).

Any individual with respect to whom an annuity is reduced under subsection 719(a) may appeal the reduction to the Director of the Office of Personnel Management pursuant to such regulations as the Director may prescribe for purposes of subsection 719(a).
unit_attributes.actor: individual with respect to whom an annuity is reduced under this subsection
unit_attributes.actor_quote: Any individual with respect to whom an annuity is reduced under this subsection

unit_attributes.statement: The Secretary may order that the covered service of an individual who the Secretary proposes to remove for performance or misconduct under section 713, 714, or 7461 of title 38 or any other provision of law but who leaves employment at the Department prior to the issuance of a final decision with respect to such action not be taken into account for calculating an annuity under chapter 83 or chapter 84 of title 5, if the Secretary determines that the individual is convicted of a felony (and the conviction is final) that influenced the individual's performance while employed in the position, and before the order is made the individual is afforded notice of the proposed order and an opportunity to respond by not later than 10 business days following receipt of notice, and the Secretary issues the order not later than 5 business days after receiving a response or not later than 15 business days after providing notice if the individual does not respond.

Upon the issuance of an order by the Secretary under section 719(b)(1), the individual shall have an opportunity to appeal the order to the Director of the Office of Personnel Management before the date that is seven business days after the date of such issuance.
The Director of the Office of Personnel Management must make a final decision with respect to an appeal under paragraph 719(b)(2) within 30 business days of receiving the appeal.
unit_attributes.actor: Director of the Office of Personnel Management
unit_attributes.actor_quote: The Director of the Office of Personnel Management

unit_attributes.statement: Not later than 37 business days after the Secretary issues a final order under subsection 719(a) or (b) with respect to an individual, the Director of the Office of Personnel Management must recalculate the annuity of the individual.
unit_attributes.actor: Director of the Office of Personnel Management
unit_attributes.actor_quote: the Director of the Office of Personnel Management

unit_attributes.statement: Any individual with respect to whom an annuity is reduced under subsection 719(a) or (b) is entitled to be paid so much of such individual's lump-sum credit as is attributable to the period of covered service.
unit_attributes.actor: individual with respect to whom an annuity is reduced under subsection (a) or (b)
unit_attributes.actor_quote: Any individual with respect to whom an annuity is reduced under subsection (a) or (b)

unit_attributes.statement: The Secretary, in consultation with the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, must prescribe regulations that may provide for the payment to the spouse or children of any individual referred to in subsection 719(a) or (b) of any amounts which (but for this subsection) would otherwise have been nonpayable by reason of such subsections; such regulations must be consistent with the requirements of section 8332(o)(6) and 8411(l)(5) of title 5, as the case may be.

In section 719, 'covered service' means, with respect to an individual subject to a removal for performance or misconduct under section 719 or 7461 of title 38 or any other provision of law, the period of service beginning on the date that the Secretary determines under such applicable provision that the individual engaged in activity that gave rise to such action and ending on the date that the individual is removed from or leaves a position of employment at the Department prior to the issuance of a final decision with respect to such action.
In section 719, 'lump-sum credit' has the meaning given such term in section 8331(8) or section 8401(19) of title 5, as the case may be.
In section 719, 'service' has the meaning given such term in section 8331(12) or section 8401(26) of title 5, as the case may be.

Section 719 of title 38, United States Code, as added by subsection 203(a)(1), applies to any action of removal of an employee of the Department of Veterans Affairs under section 719 or 7461 of such title or any other provision of law, commencing on or after June 23, 2017.

Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the Secretary may issue an order directing an employee of the Department to repay the amount, or a portion of the amount, of any award or bonus paid to the employee under title 5 (including chapters 45 or 53) or title 38 if the Secretary determines that the individual engaged in misconduct or poor performance prior to payment of the award or bonus and that such award or bonus would not have been paid (in whole or in part) had the misconduct or poor performance been known prior to payment, provided that before repayment the employee is afforded notice of the proposed order and an opportunity to respond not later than 10 business days after receipt of notice, and the Secretary issues the order not later than 5 business days after receiving a response or not later than 15 business days after providing notice if the individual does not respond.

Upon the issuance of an order by the Secretary under subsection 721(a) with respect to an individual, the individual shall have an opportunity to appeal the order to the Director of the Office of Personnel Management before the date that is seven business days after the date of such issuance.
The Director of the Office of Personnel Management must make a final decision with respect to an appeal under paragraph 721(b)(1) within 30 business days after receiving such appeal.

Section 721 of title 38, United States Code, as added by subsection 204(a), applies with respect to an award or bonus paid by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to an employee of the Department of Veterans Affairs on or after June 23, 2017.

Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the Secretary may issue an order directing an employee of the Department to repay the amount, or a portion of the amount, paid to or on behalf of the employee under title 5 for relocation expenses (including any expenses under section 5724 or 5724a of such title) or under title 38 if the Secretary determines that relocation expenses were paid following an act of fraud or malfeasance that influenced the authorization of the relocation expenses, and before repayment the employee is afforded notice of the proposed order and an opportunity to respond not later than 10 business days following receipt of notice, and the Secretary issues the order not later than 5 business days after receiving a response or not later than 15 business days after providing notice if the individual does not respond.

Upon the issuance of an order by the Secretary under subsection 723(a) with respect to an individual, the individual shall have an opportunity to appeal the order to the Director of the Office of Personnel Management before the date that is seven business days after the date of such issuance.
The Director of the Office of Personnel Management must make a final decision with respect to an appeal under paragraph 723(b)(1) within 30 days after receiving such appeal.

Section 723 of title 38, United States Code, as added by subsection 205(a), applies with respect to an amount paid by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to or on behalf of an employee of the Department of Veterans Affairs for relocation expenses on or after June 23, 2017.

The Secretary must conduct an annual performance plan for each political appointee of the Department that is similar to the annual performance plan conducted for an employee of the Department who is appointed as a career appointee (as defined in section 3132(a) of title 5) within the Senior Executive Service at the Department.

Each annual performance plan conducted under subsection 725(a) with respect to a political appointee of the Department must include an assessment of whether the appointee is meeting the goals of: (1) recruiting, selecting, and retaining well-qualified individuals for employment at the Department; (2) engaging and motivating employees; (3) training and developing employees and preparing those employees for future leadership roles within the Department; and (4) holding each employee of the Department that is a manager accountable for addressing issues relating to performance, in particular issues relating to the performance of employees that report to the manager.

In section 725, 'political appointee' means an employee of the Department who holds either a position which has been excepted from the competitive service by reason of its confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating character, or a position in the Senior Executive Service as a noncareer appointee (as defined in section 3132(a) of title 5).

Not later than 100 days after the end of each fiscal year, the Secretary must submit to the appropriate committees of Congress a report that contains, for the most recent fiscal year ending before submittal, a description of all performance awards or bonuses awarded to each Regional Office Director of the Department, Director of a Medical Center of the Department, Director of a Veterans Integrated Service Network, and Senior executive of the Department.

Each report submitted under subsection 726(a) must include, with respect to each performance award or bonus awarded to an individual described in that subsection: (1) the amount of each award or bonus; (2) the job title of the individual awarded the award or bonus; and (3) the location where the individual awarded the award or bonus works.
In section 726, 'appropriate committees of Congress' means the Committees on Veterans' Affairs and Appropriations of the Senate and House of Representatives.
In section 726, 'senior executive' means a career appointee, or an individual in an administrative or executive position who was appointed under section 7306(a) or section 7401(1) of title 38.
In section 726, 'career appointee' has the meaning given that term in section 3132(a) of title 5.

No individual employed in a senior executive position at the Department may be reassigned to another such position at the Department unless such reassignment is approved in writing and signed by the Secretary.
unit_attributes.actor: individual employed in a senior executive position at the Department
unit_attributes.actor_quote: individual employed in a senior executive position at the Department

unit_attributes.statement: Not later than June 30 and December 31 of each year, the Secretary must submit to Congress a report on the reassignment of individuals employed in senior executive positions at the Department to other such positions at the Department during the period covered by the report.
Each report submitted under paragraph 727(b)(1) must describe the purpose of each reassignment and the costs associated with such reassignment.

For purposes of paragraph 727(b)(2), costs associated with a reassignment may only include a salary increase, temporary travel expenses for the individual or the family of the individual, moving expenses, or a paid incentive.
In section 727, 'senior executive position' has the meaning given such term in section 713(d) of title 38.

The Secretary must prohibit any employee of the Department who the Secretary or the Inspector General of the Department determines has knowingly misused a purchase card from serving as a purchase card holder or approving official.
A prohibition under section 728(a)(1) against serving as a purchase card holder or approving official is in addition to any other applicable penalty.

For purposes of section 728, 'misuse' means splitting purchases, exceeding applicable purchase card limits or purchase thresholds, purchasing any unauthorized item, using a purchase card without being an authorized purchase card holder, or violating ethics standards.

In accordance with paragraph 731(a)(2), the Secretary must carry out adverse actions against supervisory employees (as defined in section 7103(a) of title 5) whom the Secretary, an administrative judge, the Merit Systems Protection Board, the Office of Special Counsel, an adjudicating body provided under a union contract, a Federal judge, or the Inspector General of the Department determines committed a prohibited personnel action described in subsection 731(c): for the first offense, an adverse action that is not less than a 12-day suspension and not more than removal; and for the second offense, removal.
An employee against whom an adverse action under paragraph 731(a)(1) is proposed is entitled to written notice.
unit_attributes.actor: employee against whom an adverse action under paragraph (1) is proposed
unit_attributes.actor_quote: An employee against whom an adverse action under paragraph (1) is proposed

unit_attributes.statement: An employee who is notified under subparagraph 731(a)(2)(A) of being the subject of a proposed adverse action under paragraph 731(a)(1) is entitled to 10 days following such notification to answer and furnish evidence in support of the answer.
unit_attributes.actor: employee who is notified under subparagraph (A) of being the subject of a proposed adverse action under paragraph (1)
unit_attributes.actor_quote: An employee who is notified under subparagraph (A) of being the subject of a proposed adverse action under paragraph (1)

unit_attributes.statement: If an employee notified of a proposed adverse action under paragraph 731(a)(1) does not furnish any evidence within 10 days, or if the Secretary determines that such evidence is not sufficient to reverse the determination to propose the adverse action, the Secretary must carry out the adverse action following such 10-day period.

Paragraphs (1) and (2) of subsection (b) of section 7513 of title 5, subsection (c) of such section, paragraphs (1) and (2) of subsection (b) of section 7543 of such title, and subsection (c) of such section do not apply with respect to an adverse action carried out under paragraph 731(a)(1).

With respect to a prohibited personnel action described in subsection 731(c), if the Secretary carries out an adverse action against a supervisory employee, the Secretary may carry out an additional adverse action under section 731 based on the same prohibited personnel action if the total severity of the adverse actions does not exceed the level specified in subsection 731(a).

A prohibited personnel action described in subsection 731(c) is any of the following actions: (1) taking or failing to take a personnel action in violation of section 2302 of title 5 against an employee relating to the employee making a whistleblower disclosure to the Assistant Secretary for Accountability and Whistleblower Protection, the Inspector General of the Department, the Special Counsel, or Congress; providing information or participating as a witness in an investigation of such a disclosure; participating in an audit or investigation by the Comptroller General of the United States; refusing to perform an action that is unlawful or prohibited by the Department; or engaging in communications related to position duties or otherwise protected; (2) preventing or restricting an employee from taking any such action; (3) conducting a negative peer review or opening a retaliatory investigation because of an employee activity protected by section 2302 of title 5; or (4) requesting a contractor to carry out an action prohibited by section 4705(b) or section 4712(a)(1) of title 41.
In section 731, 'whistleblower disclosure' has the meaning given such term in section 323(g) of title 38.

The Secretary of Veterans Affairs must provide periodic training to each employee of the Department of Veterans Affairs who is employed as a supervisor on: (1) the rights of whistleblowers and how to address a report by an employee of a hostile work environment, reprisal, or harassment; (2) how to effectively motivate, manage, and reward employees who report to the supervisor; and (3) how to effectively manage employees who are performing at an unacceptable level and access assistance from the Department's human resources office and Office of the General Counsel with respect to those employees.
In section 209 of Public Law 115-41, 'supervisor' has the meaning given such term in section 7103(a) of title 5, United States Code.
In section 209 of Public Law 115-41, 'whistleblower' has the meaning given such term in section 323(g) of title 38, United States Code, as added by section 101.

The Secretary, in consultation with the Assistant Secretary of Accountability and Whistleblower Protection, must develop criteria that the Secretary must use as a critical element in any evaluation of the performance of a supervisory employee, and that promotes the protection of whistleblowers.
